name: The Cape
positioning: The Cape, a Thompson Hotel: a design-led resort on a bluff above Monuments Beach, looking out to El Arco
best_for: Travelers who want ocean views of El Arco from a private balcony
Food-focused guests who want Manta, from chef Enrique Olvera
Groups and families wanting villas with full kitchens and plunge pools

facts.text: The Cape sits on a bluff above Monuments Beach, a local surf break.
The hotel is on the tourist corridor between Cabo San Lucas and San Jose del Cabo.
Rooms, suites and villas look out to El Arco and Bahia Cabo San Lucas.
One of the pools is an infinity pool with a swim-up bar.
Manta serves seafood from chef Enrique Olvera's exhibition-style kitchen.
Manta takes inspiration from Pacific Coast cultures, including Mexico, Peru and Japan.
The Ledge pairs modern Mexican and traditional American cooking by the beach.
The Ledge is known for its Cape Toast and a Sunday brunch with live music.
Currents Spa has al fresco cabanas, hot and cold plunge pools, a steam room and a sauna.
Interiors feature mid-century Latin American furnishings and custom sateen-woven linens.
The one-, two- and three-bedroom villas have full kitchens and plunge pools.
The Cape is pet-friendly, with restrictions.

highlights.text: The hotel has a saltwater pool carved into natural rock.
Currents Spa is set within natural rock formations.
The Rooftop has open-air bars, al fresco dining, sunken communal seating and a fire pit.
The hotel is a collaboration between Mexico City architect Javier Sanchez and interior designer Marisabel Gomez Vazquez.
Rooms have private balconies with a hanging daybed.

considerations.text: Monuments Beach below the hotel is a surf spot and not really swimmable.
The pool bar and open-air lobby play music into the night.
The spa is on the smaller side.
